trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.interpretation: The platinum is a meta-trophy: it certifies completion of the other 54 trophies on this list and asks for nothing of its own beyond them.
trophies.kitFact: The kit lists this as the single platinum of 55 and its own hint states the requirement plainly: earn the other 54 trophies.
trophies.strategy: Treat the platinum as an audit, not a grind target. Work the list by category, keep this checklist current after every session, and use the Platinum Navigator phases to catch stragglers before you declare the run finished.
steps: Earn trophies 2-55; this one has no separate objective.
After each session, tick off what popped and export a JSON backup.
When 54 are earned, confirm the count here reads 54 of 54 before expecting the platinum.
trophies.preparation: None of its own. Preparation is whatever the remaining unearned trophies require.
trophies.riskNote: Nothing in the kit suggests the platinum itself can be missed; its risk is inherited entirely from the other 54, none of which carries confirmed missable evidence.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #1 (name, description, grade as PlayStation publishes them); PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #1 (agrees on name, description and grade). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #1.

trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
trophies.guide: Finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
trophies.interpretation: A story-progression trophy tied to one named mission, Gone Fishing, which the kit hint identifies as the opening mission of the game.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the mission name Gone Fishing and, in its hint, that it is the opening mission. Nothing else about its content is established.
trophies.strategy: Play the opening as a tutorial audit: learn movement, driving and interaction prompts here, because every later system builds on them. There is no preparation possible before a first mission, so simply finish it and let the trophy register your start.
steps: Start a new game and follow the opening mission, Gone Fishing.
Complete every objective the mission presents until it ends.
Confirm the trophy pops before moving on; if it does not, replaying the opening is the only established remedy.
trophies.preparation: None possible or needed: this is the first mission.
trophies.riskNote: The kit gives no evidence that an opening mission can be skipped or locked out; story trophies are earned by completing the named content.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #2; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #2 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #2.

trophies.name: Paradise Lost
trophies.interpretation: A chapter-completion trophy: the first full chapter of the story, distinct from the opening mission tracked separately by Just Like Paradise.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a chapter structure and that completing Chapter 1 earns this bronze. It does not list which missions Chapter 1 contains.
trophies.strategy: Do not rush the chapter boundary. Before finishing Chapter 1, sweep up any early side content you have already unlocked, because the kit does not establish whether early content stays available afterwards — a caution, not a confirmed missable.
steps: Progress the story until Chapter 1 concludes.
Optionally clear already-unlocked side activities before the final Chapter 1 mission.
Verify the trophy registers at the chapter end screen or summary.
trophies.preparation: A manual save before the chapter's final mission is a cheap insurance habit, if the game offers one — save behaviour is unverified.
trophies.riskNote: No kit evidence that Chapter 1 completion can be missed; the only open question, unanswered by the kit, is whether chapter-gated side content persists.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #3; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #3 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #3.

trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
trophies.interpretation: The second chapter-completion trophy. The asterisked title is reproduced exactly as PlayStation publishes it.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms Chapter 2 exists as a discrete story unit with its own completion trophy, and gives the name with asterisks exactly as shown here.
trophies.strategy: Use Chapter 2 to start parallel progress on count-based trophies (stunts, vehicles discovered, spending) while the story is still early, so the long counters are never a late-game wall.
steps: Complete the missions grouped under Chapter 2.
Keep chipping at cumulative counters between story missions.
Confirm the trophy at the chapter's conclusion.
trophies.preparation: None established. Keeping one rolling save per chapter is prudent but unverified as a game feature.
trophies.riskNote: No evidence in the kit that a chapter can be bypassed or its trophy locked out.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #4; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #4 (both agree on the asterisked name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #4.

trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
trophies.interpretation: The third chapter-completion trophy, continuing the chapter sequence that runs from Paradise Lost through to the final mission trophy.
trophies.kitFact: The kit establishes Chapter 3 as a discrete unit with a bronze completion trophy. It does not name the chapter's missions.
trophies.strategy: By Chapter 3 the map and activity set should be widening. Alternate one story push with one activity session (races, shooting range, stunts) so skill-based silvers improve gradually instead of becoming an endgame cram.
steps: Finish Chapter 3's story missions.
Rotate in activity trophies between missions to build long-term progress.
Verify the trophy registers when the chapter closes.
trophies.preparation: None established by the kit.
trophies.riskNote: No kit evidence of a missable condition for chapter completion.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #5; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #5 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #5.

trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
trophies.interpretation: The fourth chapter-completion trophy — the last chapter trophy on the list before the separate final-mission gold, You Gotta Know When to Get Off.
trophies.kitFact: The kit lists four chapter trophies (Chapters 1-4) and a separate final-mission trophy, so Chapter 4 is not itself the ending.
trophies.strategy: Treat the end of Chapter 4 as the point of no return rehearsal: before pushing into the finale stretch, audit this checklist for strand finales (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy, Tyrone) and start any you have not, in case availability changes — the kit neither confirms nor denies that it does.
steps: Complete Chapter 4.
Audit side-strand progress before continuing the story.
Confirm the trophy, then proceed toward the final mission.
trophies.preparation: A checklist audit at this milestone; no in-game preparation is established.
trophies.riskNote: Strictly, no missable is evidenced. The audit step above is a precaution against an unverified possibility, not a response to a confirmed one.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #6; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #6 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #6.

trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
trophies.interpretation: The story's finishing trophy and one of only two golds on the list: complete the final mission, whatever form it takes.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a final mission exists, that it is distinct from Chapter 4, and that completing it earns gold. It does not name the mission.
trophies.strategy: Before starting the finale, finish anything you personally would hate to redo and export a backup of this checklist. If the game offers choices near the end, the only choice-sensitive trophy on the list (Actions Speak Louder) is tracked separately — this trophy's text asks only for completion.
steps: Reach and start the final mission.
Complete it through to the story's conclusion.
Confirm the gold registers; keep playing afterwards for the 100% completion gold if free roam continues.
trophies.preparation: Checklist backup exported; strand finales reviewed. Whether post-story free roam exists is unverified.
trophies.riskNote: The description conditions the trophy on completing the final mission only. No branching or missable condition is evidenced by the kit.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #7; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #7 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #7.

steps: Reach the mission Breakfast Run in story progression.
Complete all of its objectives.
Confirm the bronze pops at mission end.

Complete the mission to its end.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.interpretation: The second gold: reach 100% game completion as the game itself measures it. This is broader than the trophy list — many of its components will not have trophies of their own.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a 100% completion statistic exists and that attaining it earns gold. It does not enumerate what counts toward the percentage.
trophies.strategy: Work from the game's own completion checklist, not this trophy list: finish the story, then strands, activities, collectibles and exploration, checking the in-game percentage after each block. Expect the last few percent to be unglamorous leftovers — log them in the journal here as you find them.
steps: Complete the story and all strand finales.
Clear activities, collectibles and exploration trophies, which overlap heavily with completion.
Track the in-game percentage to exactly 100% and confirm the gold.
trophies.preparation: A running journal of what raised the percentage is the single most useful tool; the kit does not supply the component list.
trophies.riskNote: No component is evidenced as missable. If any component were one-time-only, that would matter — but the kit establishes no such component, so the honest classification is no missable evidence.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.interpretation: A cumulative counter trophy: complete 250 stunts, however the game defines and counts a stunt. It is a volume trophy, not a skill-peak trophy.
trophies.kitFact: The kit fixes the target at exactly 250 stunts and the grade at silver. It does not define what qualifies as one stunt.
trophies.strategy: Start early and never do a driving session without banking a few. Spread over the whole playthrough, 250 is roughly a handful per hour; left to the end, it is a repetitive wall. When you find a reliable stunt spot, note it in the journal rather than trusting memory.
steps: Learn what the game counts as a stunt from its own feedback.
Weave stunts into ordinary travel instead of dedicated-only sessions.
Check the counter periodically and push the final stretch at a repeatable spot you have logged.
trophies.preparation: One logged, repeatable stunt location of your own discovery; the kit names none.
trophies.riskNote: A repeatable counter; nothing suggests stunts become unavailable.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.interpretation: A sampler trophy: attempt every type of activity the game offers, once each. The kit hint puts the number of activity types at 9.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms 9 activity types and that trying each once earns this bronze. It does not name the 9 types.
trophies.strategy: Use this as your map of the game's side content: each time a new activity icon or venue appears, try it immediately and tick a private tally. The other activity trophies (races, fishing, arcade, shooting range) prove at least four of the types; the rest you must discover by exploring.
steps: Try each new activity type the first time you encounter it.
Keep a journal tally until you reach 9 distinct types.
If the trophy has not popped at 9, an activity tried during a mission may not have counted — retry it in free roam.
trophies.preparation: None; curiosity is the requirement.
trophies.riskNote: Activities are repeatable world content; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #16; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #16 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 9-type count is the kit hint). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #16.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.interpretation: A mastery trophy: every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them per the kit hint — must be finished at gold-medal standard, not merely completed.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the Shooting Range exists, holds 42 challenges, and that gold medals in all of them earn this silver. Medal thresholds are not given.
trophies.strategy: Do not save the range for the end. Clear each challenge to gold while its weapon class is fresh, and treat a near-miss as information: note the score gap in the journal and re-run immediately rather than moving on. If a challenge resists, change one variable at a time — weapon, position, pacing — because the kit gives no official technique, and disciplined iteration is the honest substitute.
steps: Unlock the Shooting Range and survey all 42 challenges.
Gold them in groups per weapon or style, logging stubborn ones in the journal.
Re-run logged near-misses until every challenge shows gold, then confirm the silver.
trophies.preparation: Patience and a per-challenge score log. No loadout or unlock requirement is established by the kit.
trophies.riskNote: Range challenges are repeatable by design; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #17; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #17 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 42-challenge count is the kit hint, matching the count PlayStation tracks). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #17.

Add and win each new location's race as exploration reveals it.

trophies.strategy: Keep a wins list with race names in the journal; distinctness is the whole challenge. Prioritise entering every new race you unlock once, rather than re-running favourites, and only grind repeats for cash if the economy demands it.

Enter each newly unlocked race promptly and log every distinct win.

trophies.name: Spin On This!
trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.interpretation: Tyrone's strand-finale trophy, the fifth named strand finale on the list alongside Andy, Kenton, Billy and Randy.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms Tyrone as a strand character whose final mission earns this bronze. Strand content is unstated.
trophies.strategy: Finish Tyrone's strand like the others and keep the set together in your journal: these five finales plus three more strands complete the Strangers & Freaks silver, so this bronze is worth double progress.
steps: Open Tyrone's strand when it appears.
Complete the strand's missions.
Finish the final mission and confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: Tyrone's earlier missions; count not established.
trophies.riskNote: No missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #27; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #27 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #27.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.interpretation: A coverage trophy: meditation spots exist across Leonida — 18 of them per the kit hint — and you must meditate at every one.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms meditation as an activity, 18 spots, and statewide distribution. It names no spot locations.
trophies.strategy: This is a found-set trophy: the danger is the last two spots, not the first sixteen. Log each spot's rough area in the journal the moment you use it, and when exploring a new region, look for quiet, scenic or elevated places — meditation spots are placed where a player would plausibly stop, though that placement logic is inference, not kit fact.
steps: Meditate at the first spot you find and start the tally.
Add each new spot as exploration reveals it, logging its area.
At 18 of 18, confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: A spot log; the kit provides no map.
trophies.riskNote: World spots are persistent content; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #28; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #28 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 18-spot count is the kit hint). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #28.

trophies.name: Fair Game
trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt the unique animal for Bret.
trophies.interpretation: A one-target hunting task for a character named Bret: hunt a unique — singular, specific — animal. Which animal, and where, the kit does not say.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a character Bret, a hunting activity, and one unique animal as the target. Species and location are unstated.
trophies.strategy: Take Bret's task when offered and treat it as a tracking exercise: unique-animal hunts usually hinge on finding sign or a habitat rather than combat difficulty, but that is genre inference. If the hunt stalls, re-read the task's in-game wording — the description here is all the evidence that exists outside the game.
steps: Accept Bret's hunting task.
Track and hunt the unique animal it specifies.
Complete the hunt and confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: Whatever hunting tools the game provides; no specific gear is established.
trophies.riskNote: No evidence the task can fail permanently; a unique target might be re-attemptable, but that is unverified.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #29; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #29 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #29.

trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
trophies.interpretation: A set-completion trophy: collectible cards are grouped into sets, and completing any 3 full sets earns the silver. Total set count and cards per set are not given.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms collectible cards, a set structure, and a target of 3 completed sets. It does not say how many sets or cards exist.
trophies.strategy: Focus fire: finish the three sets you are closest to rather than spreading pickups evenly. Log cards by set in the journal — with collectibles, the expensive mistake is not knowing which set a missing card belongs to. Buy or trade mechanics, if any exist, are unverified; assume found-in-world until the game shows otherwise.
steps: Start collecting cards and record them by set.
Push your three most-complete sets to full.
Confirm the silver at 3 completed sets.
trophies.preparation: A per-set card log is strongly advised; the kit supplies no card list.
trophies.riskNote: Collectibles are persistent world items; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #30; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #30 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #30.

trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
trophies.interpretation: Perform an action the game calls WAiNK It at 100 distinct locations. The kit never defines WAiNK It — what the action is must be learned from the game itself.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the action name WAiNK It, a target of 100 locations, and silver grade. The action's nature is genuinely not established anywhere in the kit.
trophies.strategy: First, discover what WAiNK It is from in-game prompts, tutorials or menus; until then no route planning is possible. Once known, treat it like the meditation spots: log locations as you go, because a 100-count coverage trophy is lost or won on bookkeeping, not skill.
steps: Identify the WAiNK It action from the game's own teaching.
Perform it at each new location you visit and keep a tally.
At 100 locations, confirm the silver.
trophies.preparation: A location tally once the action is understood; nothing can be prepared before that.
trophies.riskNote: A repeatable location action; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #31; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #31 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 100-location count is the kit hint). The meaning of WAiNK It is UNVERIFIED in the kit. Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #31.

trophies.name: One Last Thing
trophies.interpretation: Complete 50 challenges — a general challenge system distinct from the Shooting Range challenges, though whether range challenges count toward the 50 is not stated.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a challenges system and a target of 50 completions. It does not enumerate challenge types or say how they overlap with other systems.
trophies.strategy: Challenges usually accumulate passively if you engage with everything; the risk is finishing the game at 43 of 50 with no plan. Check the challenge count whenever you check this list, and if you are short late, farm the shortest repeatable challenges the game offers — which ones those are must be learned in-game.
steps: Note your challenge count early so its growth is visible.
Complete challenges opportunistically across all activities.
Top up to 50 with quick repeatables if needed, then confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: Periodic count checks; no specific challenge is established as optimal.
trophies.riskNote: Challenge systems are repeatable; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #32; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #32 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #32.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Lose a 4-star wanted level with your partner.
trophies.interpretation: A co-presence crime trophy: while with your partner, reach a 4-star wanted level and then lose it — escape — with the partner still with you.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a partner mechanic, a wanted-level system reaching at least 4 stars, and that losing the level with the partner present earns this bronze.
trophies.strategy: Engineer it deliberately: with your partner present, commit enough minor crime in a low-risk area to hit exactly the wanted level you need, then break line of sight and hide until it clears. Do not improvise this during a mission — set it up in free roam where failure costs nothing. The escape method details are gameplay, not kit fact; adapt to what the game teaches about its wanted system.
steps: Have your partner with you in free roam.
Raise the wanted level to 4 stars.
Evade until the level is fully lost, partner still present, and confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: Partner present and a planned escape area; specific wanted-system mechanics are unverified.
trophies.riskNote: A repeatable free-roam setup; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #33; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #33 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #33.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner, keeping your wanted level.
trophies.interpretation: A chained crime trophy: rob 3 shops consecutively with your partner, and — counterintuitively — your wanted level must not be lost between them; the chain happens under continuous heat.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms shop robbery, the partner mechanic, a 3-shop chain, and the condition that the wanted level persists throughout. It pairs naturally with Hot Together, which wants the opposite: losing the level.
trophies.strategy: Plan a three-shop route in one neighbourhood before starting, so travel under heat is short. Rob shop one, move directly to shop two and three without hiding long enough to drop the level, and only evade afterwards — conveniently, that final escape with your partner is exactly what Hot Together rewards, so attempt both in one sequence: chain first, escape second.
steps: Scout 3 nearby shops with your partner present.
Rob all 3 consecutively, keeping the wanted level alive between them.
Escape afterwards and confirm the bronze (and likely Hot Together).
trophies.preparation: A pre-scouted 3-shop cluster. The pairing with Hot Together is LEONIDA's reading of the two descriptions, not a confirmed dependency.
trophies.riskNote: Repeatable in free roam; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #34; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #34 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #34.

trophies.name: Whip It Good
trophies.interpretation: Discover 100 distinct vehicles — a catalogue trophy. Discovery most plausibly means encountering or entering a vehicle model for the first time, but the kit does not define it.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a vehicle-discovery counter with a target of 100. The discovery trigger (see, enter, drive, own) is not specified.
trophies.strategy: Variety is the method: drive something different whenever the option appears, visit richer and poorer districts alike since vehicle pools usually vary by area — area-pool variation is genre inference — and log models in the journal if the game does not show a discovered list. Airport, port and rural traffic are prime hunting grounds in this kind of game; verify in-game.
steps: Start noting distinct vehicles from the first hour.
Deliberately sample vehicles in each new district and setting.
At 100 discovered, confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: A model log if the game lacks a visible catalogue; the kit does not confirm one exists.
trophies.riskNote: World traffic is persistent; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #35; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #35 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #35.

trophies.name: Gunslinger
trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Down 5 enemies in one Combat Focus.
trophies.interpretation: A single-window skill trophy: during one activation of an ability called Combat Focus, take down 5 enemies. The ability's exact behaviour is defined by the game, not the kit.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms an ability named Combat Focus and a 5-takedown requirement inside one use. Duration, cooldown and unlock point are unstated.
trophies.strategy: Do not waste activations on scattered pairs. Wait for a grouped encounter — five or more enemies in one area — line up the weakest targets first, and trigger Combat Focus only when all five are reachable within its window. If an attempt lands at 4, note the encounter in the journal; repeatable group fights are the farming spots for this.
steps: Unlock Combat Focus and learn its window in easy fights.
Find an encounter with at least 5 grouped enemies.
Activate once and take down 5 before it ends; confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: A known grouped encounter. Ability mechanics must be learned in-game; none are established by the kit.
trophies.riskNote: Combat encounters recur; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #36; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #36 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #36.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Leave VCIA in an unscheduled way.
trophies.interpretation: At VCIA — the location of the VCIA Takedown mission — depart in an unscheduled way: in plain terms, leave by an aircraft or route that was not scheduled, most plausibly by taking a plane you were not booked on. The exact trigger is the game's to define.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms VCIA as a place, an unscheduled-departure action, and the bronze for doing it. It does not expand VCIA or specify the vehicle involved.
trophies.strategy: Visit VCIA in free roam, ideally after VCIA Takedown has taught you the layout, and experiment: board or take an aircraft you have no ticket for, or exit through a non-passenger route. If nothing triggers, the moment may be scripted inside a mission — journal what you tried so attempts are not repeated blindly.
steps: Go to VCIA in free roam and survey aircraft and exits.
Attempt an unscheduled departure: take an unbooked aircraft or non-standard exit.
If it does not register, watch for a scripted opportunity during VCIA-related missions and take it.
trophies.preparation: Familiarity with VCIA from the Takedown mission helps; the pairing is from the kit's own text.
trophies.riskNote: No evidence VCIA access is lost after its mission; if the trigger were mission-scripted only, risk would rise — that possibility is unverified, so the classification stays at no missable evidence with this caveat recorded.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #37; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #37 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #37.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.interpretation: The vaguest combat trophy on the list. Rhinos are tanks (the kit hint says so); kinda hot in these Rhinos suggests spending time in one, or surviving heat inside one — but the actual trigger is not stated anywhere.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms only that Rhinos are tanks and that something done with them earns this bronze. The verb — drive, survive, destroy, steal — is not given.
trophies.strategy: When you first get access to a Rhino, experiment systematically and journal each attempt: enter one, drive one, survive a wanted level in one, destroy one. One of the obvious interactions is very likely the trigger; the honest position is that nobody can plan this precisely from the available evidence, so methodical trials replace a route.
steps: Gain access to a Rhino tank.
Try the plausible interactions in turn: enter, drive, fight, survive, destroy.
Record which interaction pops the trophy in the journal for other players.
trophies.preparation: Access to a Rhino, whenever the game provides it; the source of one is unverified.
trophies.riskNote: The objective is too vague to assess risk: with no stated trigger, no missable condition can be confirmed or excluded. Classified UNKNOWN strictly from lack of evidence.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #38; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #38 (both agree on name and description as PlayStation publishes them; the description itself is a joke line with no stated action). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #38.

trophies.name: Sneakthief
trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being seen.
trophies.interpretation: A stealth robbery trophy: rob a jewelry store and complete the robbery undetected. Detection rules — cameras, witnesses, alarms — are the game's, not the kit's.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms jewelry stores can be robbed and that an undetected robbery earns this bronze. It does not define detection.
trophies.strategy: Case the target first: entrances, staff positions, and whatever detection sources the game shows. Attempt it at the quietest in-game moment you can find, move efficiently, and leave before any response escalates. If an attempt is blown, learn which sense detected you and change that variable only — stealth trophies reward iteration, and failed attempts cost nothing if you reload or walk away.
steps: Scout a jewelry store's layout and detection sources.
Enter and complete the robbery without triggering detection.
Exit cleanly and confirm the bronze; retry with one changed variable if detected.
trophies.preparation: A scouted store and a save beforehand if available. Detection mechanics are unverified and must be learned in-game.
trophies.riskNote: Stores are persistent world locations and robberies repeatable; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #39; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #39 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #39.

trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal
trophies.interpretation: Rob 5 bank vaults — distinct, major robberies, not shop tills — and escape after each. The escape is part of the requirement, so a vault robbery that ends in arrest or death plausibly does not count.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms bank vaults as robbery targets, a count of 5, an escape condition, and silver grade. Vault locations are not listed.
trophies.strategy: Treat each vault as a small heist: scout the location, plan the exit route before entering, and keep the escape vehicle staged if the game allows. Log completed vaults by location in the journal — with exactly 5 required, one forgotten success can send you re-robbing a vault that no longer counts. Pair escapes with your partner when possible to keep partner-trophy habits warm, though no pairing is required here.
steps: Find and scout a bank vault location.
Rob it and escape cleanly; log the location.
Repeat at 5 distinct vaults and confirm the silver.
trophies.preparation: Per-vault scouting and an escape plan. Whether the same vault can be re-robbed for credit is unverified — assume distinct vaults.
trophies.riskNote: Bank robberies are repeatable world crime; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #40; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #40 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #40.

trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape.
trophies.interpretation: A single-event crime trophy: rob one armored truck and escape afterwards. One success is enough.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms armored trucks exist as robbery targets and that robbing one plus escaping earns this bronze. How trucks are found or opened is unstated.
trophies.strategy: When you spot an armored truck in traffic or parked, commit: disable or access it by whatever method the game presents, take the money, and prioritise the escape over extra loot. Because only one is needed, do not pass up the first opportunity waiting for a perfect setup — an adequate attempt teaches the mechanics, and trucks recur.
steps: Spot an armored truck in the world.
Rob it using the interaction the game offers.
Escape the response and confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: A fast escape vehicle nearby helps in practice; no requirement is established.
trophies.riskNote: Trucks are recurring world spawns; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #41; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #41 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #41.

trophies.name: The Goodtime State
trophies.interpretation: Full-map exploration: visit all of Leonida, which the kit hint divides into 52 areas. An area presumably counts when entered, not when completed.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the state is called Leonida, that exploration is tracked, and that there are 52 areas. Area boundaries and names are not given.
trophies.strategy: Explore region by region as the story opens the map, and keep a rough area log. The last missing areas are typically small pockets between landmarks — when stuck near the end, sweep the map edges, islands and interiors systematically rather than re-driving the centre. If the game shows an explored-areas count anywhere, mirror it in the journal after each session.
steps: Explore each new region thoroughly as it becomes accessible.
Log areas visited; watch for gaps between regions.
At 52 of 52 areas, confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: An area log; the kit provides no area list or map.
trophies.riskNote: The world remains explorable; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #42; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #42 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 52-area count is the kit hint). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #42.

trophies.name: Pest Control
trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation of each of the 9 gangs.
trophies.interpretation: Breadth-over-depth crime: there are 9 gangs, each running illegal operations, and you must rob at least one operation belonging to each gang — 9 robberies minimum, spread across all factions.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms 9 gangs, that each has illegal operations, and that robbing one per gang earns this bronze. Gang names and territories are not given.
trophies.strategy: The bookkeeping is the trophy: log every operation robbery with its owning gang, because robbing a tenth operation of a gang you have already covered adds nothing. When exploring a new territory, identify whose ground it is before hitting an operation there, and prioritise gangs still missing from your list.
steps: Rob an illegal operation and record the owning gang.
Repeat across territories until all 9 gangs are covered.
Confirm the bronze at 9 of 9 gangs.
trophies.preparation: A per-gang robbery log is essential; the kit names no gangs or territories.
trophies.riskNote: Operations are world content; no evidence any gang's operation becomes unavailable.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #43; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #43 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 9-gang count is the kit hint). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #43.

trophies.name: In The Beginning…
trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Have a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.interpretation: A place-and-action moment trophy: at Ocean Beach, have a cocktail somewhere with a view. It rewards stopping to do a small specific thing in a named location.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a location called Ocean Beach and a cocktail-with-a-view action there. The exact spot or venue is not specified.
trophies.strategy: When you reach Ocean Beach, look for bars, terraces or rooftop spots overlooking the water and use the drink interaction. If several venues exist, try the most elevated or beachfront one first — with a view is the only qualifier given, so the intended spot is the one where the view is unmistakable.
steps: Travel to Ocean Beach.
Find a bar or terrace with a clear view and order or take a cocktail.
Confirm the bronze registers at the moment of the drink.
trophies.preparation: None beyond reaching Ocean Beach.
trophies.riskNote: A repeatable world interaction; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #44; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #44 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #44.

trophies.name: Capital Offense
trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Smash out of a vehicle showroom in style.
trophies.interpretation: Drive a vehicle out through a showroom's glass — smash your way out of a vehicle showroom rather than leaving by the door. Classic style is flavour; the smash is the requirement.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms vehicle showrooms exist and that smashing out of one earns this bronze. Which showroom, and whether any vehicle qualifies, is unstated.
trophies.strategy: Enter a showroom, get into a vehicle inside, and drive it out through the window or glass frontage instead of the entrance. If the first showroom's stock cannot be driven, try another — dealership-style locations recur in this kind of map, though their count is unverified. Do it in free roam so the wanted response costs nothing.
steps: Find a vehicle showroom with vehicles inside.
Get in one and drive out through the glass.
Confirm the bronze; try another showroom if it does not register.
trophies.preparation: None established.
trophies.riskNote: Showrooms are persistent locations; no missable condition is evidenced.

trophies.name: Let’s Go Bowling
trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Play bowling at the Kolt & Associates alley.
trophies.interpretation: Play bowling at one specific venue: the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Follow-through suggests completing a game or at least bowling properly, not merely entering the building.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a bowling activity and a named venue, Kolt & Associates' bowling alley. Whether a full game, a strike, or a single throw is required is not stated.

steps: Find the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
Start a bowling game there.
Play it through and confirm the bronze.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: A partnership moment with mass appeal.
trophies.interpretation: A deliberately cryptic trophy: something about a partnership that appeals to a crowd or an audience. No action, location or count is stated — this is one of the list's riddle trophies, designed to be discovered rather than planned.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms only the trophy's existence and its riddle description. Even its hint merely restates the riddle. No mechanic is established.
trophies.strategy: There is no honest route to plan. Play with your partner present, try partner activities and public or performance-flavoured interactions, and journal anything that draws a crowd reaction. When it pops unexpectedly — riddle trophies usually do — record exactly what you were doing so the discovery becomes evidence for the next player.
steps: Keep your partner involved in varied activities.
Attempt public or audience-facing partner moments as you find them.
When it triggers, journal the precise circumstances.
trophies.preparation: None possible from available evidence.
trophies.riskNote: With no stated trigger, missability cannot be assessed; classified UNKNOWN strictly from absence of evidence.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make choices (PSN tracks a count to 500).
trophies.interpretation: A choice-volume trophy: the game tracks choices made, and PlayStation tracks a count to 500 per the kit hint. Choices made (for better or worse) — the wording says any choices count, not correct ones.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms a choices mechanic, that PlayStation tracks a count, and that the count target is 500. What qualifies as one choice is defined by the game, not the kit.
trophies.strategy: This is the list's only choice-sensitive trophy, and its demand is volume, not wisdom: never skip an optional choice prompt, dialogue decision or branching interaction, because 500 is a large number if choices are scarce. Log your count growth per chapter in the journal; if growth stalls, you are bypassing choice points somewhere and should slow down in dialogue and missions.
steps: Take every choice prompt the game offers, including optional ones.
Check the tracked count periodically against a 500 target.
If the count stalls, revisit how you handle dialogues and branching moments until it climbs again.
trophies.preparation: Attention, not equipment: the preparation is noticing choice points. Their frequency is unverified.
trophies.riskNote: Classified CHOICE-SENSITIVE from the description's own words — the trophy is literally about choices. That is not the same as confirmed missable: nothing says a choice can lock the trophy, only that progress depends on choices being made.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #48; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #48 (both agree on name and description as PlayStation publishes them; the count to 500 is the kit hint describing PlayStation's tracking). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #48.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.interpretation: Another riddle: succeed at something on a second try — fail once, then succeed at the same thing. What the something is, the kit never says.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the trophy and its fail-then-succeed shape only. The activity involved is not identified.
trophies.strategy: You cannot schedule genuine failure, but you can notice the pattern: whenever you retry anything — a race, a challenge, a mission segment — and succeed on the immediate second attempt, check whether this popped. If you want to hunt it deliberately, pick a short repeatable challenge, fail it once on purpose, then complete it; whether that qualifies depends on the game's hidden definition, which is unverified.
steps: Stay alert after any fail-then-succeed sequence in normal play.
Optionally test the theory on a short challenge: fail once, then succeed.
Journal the trigger if it pops, converting a riddle into evidence.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.interpretation: Witness something strange — an unusual event or sighting somewhere in Leonida. The X-Files-flavoured title implies the uncanny, but the kit specifies neither event nor location.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms only that witnessing something strange earns this bronze. No event, place or time is established.
trophies.strategy: Exploration is the strategy: strange events in open worlds hide off the beaten path, at night, and in places the story never sends you. Combine the hunt with The Goodtime State's full-map exploration, investigate anything that looks deliberately odd, and journal candidate spots with times — if an event is time-dependent, your log is how you will ever know.
steps: Explore beyond story routes, including remote areas.
Investigate unusual sights or events when encountered, at varied times of day.
Journal any strange event and whether the trophy registered.
trophies.preparation: None possible from available evidence; curiosity and a log substitute for a route.
trophies.riskNote: Event and trigger undefined, so missability cannot be assessed: UNKNOWN, strictly from absence of evidence.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by.
trophies.interpretation: From a moving vehicle, knock someone down with a melee attack — a drive-by performed with melee rather than a firearm. Despite the bowling name, it has nothing to do with the bowling alley trophy.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms the melee drive-by action and that knocking someone down with it earns this bronze. Vehicle and weapon specifics are unstated.
trophies.strategy: Find a slow street with pedestrians, drive at modest speed — fast enough to be a drive-by, slow enough to connect — and use the melee attack from the vehicle as you pass a target. If the game restricts melee from certain vehicles, switch vehicle type and retry; the mechanic's exact form must be learned in-game, and one clean knockdown is all it asks.
steps: Enter a vehicle and find a pedestrian at a safe, slow stretch.
Drive past and strike them with melee from the vehicle.
Confirm the bronze on the knockdown.
trophies.preparation: A suitable vehicle and street; melee-from-vehicle controls are unverified and learned in-game.
trophies.riskNote: Repeatable anywhere with traffic and pedestrians; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #51; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #51 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #51.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.interpretation: A money-flow trophy with a specific channel: earn $250,000 by laundering marked bills through your contacts. Not all income counts — only laundered marked bills, per the wording.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms marked bills, laundering through contacts, and a $250,000 target. How marked bills are obtained is not stated.
trophies.strategy: Identify the laundering loop early — which activities yield marked bills and which contact launders them — then run that loop as your default income until the counter clears. Keep a running total in the journal if the game does not display one; spending the money is fine, since the wording says earn, but verify that reading in-game before a big purchase if the counter is visible.
steps: Discover how marked bills are earned and which contact launders them.
Route income through laundering until $250,000 is reached.
Confirm the bronze at the threshold.
trophies.preparation: The laundering contact unlocked; acquisition methods for marked bills are unverified and learned in-game.
trophies.riskNote: An earnable, repeatable money loop; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #52; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #52 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #52.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.interpretation: A cumulative spending trophy: spend $100,000 in total across all shops. Any shops count — the wording pools every store's till.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms shop spending is tracked and the target is $100,000 across all shops. What shops sell is unstated.
trophies.strategy: Never hoard cash out of habit: buy the useful things — vehicles, property services, gear, customisation — as you play, and this accrues naturally alongside Little Boxes and Dime on the Dollar. If you reach the endgame short, buy big-ticket items you actually want rather than junk; there is no evidence reselling is penalised, but there is no need to test it.
steps: Spend normally on useful purchases from early on.
Check your cumulative spend whenever the game shows it.
Top up to $100,000 with worthwhile big purchases if needed, then confirm the bronze.
trophies.preparation: A healthy income loop; see Dime on the Dollar for the laundering economy the kit does establish.
trophies.riskNote: Spending is always available while shops exist; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #53; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #53 (both agree on name, description and grade as PlayStation publishes them). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #53.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.interpretation: Buy every garage property in the game — 8 of them per the kit hint. A purchase-completion trophy gated by money, not by finding secrets.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms garage properties are purchasable and that there are 8. Prices and locations are not given.
trophies.strategy: Budget for this from mid-game: garages are likely among the larger purchases, so run the laundering loop (Dime on the Dollar) and avoid draining cash on consumables when a garage is nearly affordable. Log each purchase location in the journal; the last unpurchased garage is found by elimination, not by memory.
steps: Buy each garage property as it becomes affordable.
Log all 8 purchases by location.
Confirm the bronze when the set is complete.
trophies.preparation: Sufficient cash — total cost is not established, so keep a reserve rather than spending to zero.
trophies.riskNote: Properties remain purchasable; no missable condition is evidenced.
trophies.citation: Exophase GTA VI trophy list, entry #54; PSNProfiles GTA VI trophy list, entry #54 (both agree on name, description and grade; the 8-garage count is the kit hint). Local copy: competition kit dataset, trophy #54.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles in the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.interpretation: Use an in-game app called Scooter Bros to register 10 vehicles. Registration presumably attaches vehicles to you in some way; the kit does not explain the app's purpose beyond this trophy.
trophies.kitFact: The kit confirms an app named Scooter Bros, a vehicle-registration action, and a target of 10 vehicles. Eligibility rules for vehicles are unstated.
trophies.strategy: Register vehicles as you acquire or discover them rather than in one endgame batch: registration may require ownership, condition, or proximity — all unverified — so testing it on your first vehicles teaches the rules cheaply. Pair it with Whip It Good's discovery habit: every new vehicle is a candidate for both counters.
steps: Open the Scooter Bros app and learn its registration flow on your first vehicle.
Register each new vehicle you obtain, up to 10.
Confirm the bronze at 10 registered.
trophies.preparation: Access to the Scooter Bros app and vehicles to register; eligibility rules are learned in-game.
trophies.riskNote: Vehicles and the app persist; no missable condition is evidenced.
